rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Angling[end_header][start_subHeader]Angling means take of fish by hook and line with the line held in the hand, or with the line attached to a pole or rod held in the hand or closely attended in such manner that the fish voluntarily takes the bait or artificial lure inside its mouth.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Angling
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Artificial Lure[end_header][start_subHeader]Any manufactured or man-made non-scented/flavored (regardless if scent is added in the manufacturing process or added afterwards) device complete with hooks, intended to attract fish. Artificial lures include, but are not limited to spoons, spinners, artificial flies, and plugs, made of metal, plastic, wood, or other non-edible materials.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Artificial Lure
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Authorization for Taking Fish[end_header][start_subHeader]Fish, amphibians, reptiles, mollusks and crustaceans may be taken only in the amounts, only during the open season and only with the gear authorized and shall not be taken otherwise.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Authorization for Taking Fish
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Bag and Possession Limit[end_header][start_subHeader]No more than one daily bag limit of each kind of fish, amphibian, reptile, mollusk or crustacean named in these regulations may be taken or possessed by any one person unless otherwise authorized; regardless of whether they are fresh, frozen, or otherwise preserved.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Bag and Possession Limit
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Bait[end_header][start_subHeader]Any natural or manufactured product or device which is used to attract fish by the sense of taste or smell, including any product or device to which scents or flavored attractants have been added or externally applied. Bait includes, but is not limited to; scented and flavored paste, scented manufactured fish eggs, and traditional organic baits such as worms, grubs, crickets, leeches, stink baits, insects, crayfish, human food, fish, fish parts, and fish eggs.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Bait
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Barbless Hook[end_header][start_subHeader]A fish hook from which the barb or barbs have been removed or completely bent closed, or which is manufactured without barbs.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Barbless Hook
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Black Bass[end_header][start_subHeader]Includes largemouth, small mouth, redeye and spotted  bass.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Black Bass
rows.Tags: Fin Fish - General

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Bow and Arrow Fishing Tackle[end_header][start_subHeader]Such tackle must have the arrow shaft or the point, or both, attached by a line to the bow or to a fishing reel (includes crossbow).[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Bow and Arrow Fishing Tackle
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Bullfrog[end_header][start_subHeader]Includes only Rana catesbeiana. See Chapter 5 for amphibian regulations.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Bullfrog
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Bullhead[end_header][start_subHeader]Includes brown, black and yellow bullhead.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Bullhead
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Catfish[end_header][start_subHeader]Includes channel, white, blue and flathead catfish.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Catfish
rows.Tags: Fin Fish - General

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Chumming[end_header][start_subHeader]Placing any material in the water, other than on a hook while angling, for the purpose of attracting fish to a particular area in order that they may be taken.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Chumming
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Closed or Closure[end_header][start_subHeader]Refers to waters or areas closed to all fishing unless otherwise authorized.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Closed or Closure
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Closed Season[end_header][start_subHeader]That period during which the taking of fish, amphibians, reptiles, mollusks or crustaceans is prohibited.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Closed Season
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Dates[end_header][start_subHeader]Dates of seasons and closures are inclusive.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Dates
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Dip Net[end_header][start_subHeader]Webbing supported by a frame, and hand held, not more than six feet in greatest dimension, excluding handle.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Dip Net
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Dividing Line Between Lake and Stream[end_header][start_subHeader]The mouth of the stream at the existing level of the lake surface. Stream regulations apply to parts of streams in the exposed beds of partially empty lakes.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Dividing Line Between Lake and Stream
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Filleting of Salmonids in Inland Waters[end_header][start_subHeader]Except as otherwise required, all salmon and steelhead taken in inland anadromous waters where a sport fishing license is required, must be kept in such a condition that species and size can be determined until placed at the angler's permanent residence, a commercial preservation facility or being prepared for immediate consumption. Also when required, the presence or absence of a healed adipose fin scar must be able to be determined until placed at the anglers permanent residence, a commercial preservation facility, or being prepared for immediate consumption.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Filleting of Salmonids in Inland Waters
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: Exceptions:
rows.Title: Filleting of Salmonids in Inland Waters
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: Chinook salmon taken from July 1 through December 31 in the following areas:
rows.Title: Filleting of Salmonids in Inland Waters
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: The main stem of the American and Feather rivers.
rows.Title: Filleting of Salmonids in Inland Waters
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: The main stem of the Sacramento River between the Deschutes Road Bridge and Tower Bridge.
rows.Title: Filleting of Salmonids in Inland Waters
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: Definitions
rows.Title: Filleting of Salmonids in Inland Waters
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Finfish Defined[end_header][start_subHeader]Finfish are defined as any species of bony fish or cartilaginous fish (sharks, skates and rays). Finfish do not include amphibians, invertebrates, plants or algae.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Finfish Defined
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Inland Waters[end_header][start_subHeader]Inland waters are all the fresh, brackish and inland saline waters of the state, including lagoons and tidewaters upstream from the mouths of coastal rivers and streams. Inland waters exclude open or enclosed bays contiguous to the ocean including the waters of San Francisco Bay and the waters of Elkhorn Slough, west of Elkhorn Road between Castroville and Watsonville. See Section 27.00 for the description of San Francisco Bay.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Inland Waters
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Inland Sport Fishing Districts[end_header][start_subHeader]Inland Sport Fishing Districts are defined in Sections 6.31 to 6.37 of these regulations.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Inland Sport Fishing Districts
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Lake[end_header][start_subHeader]Includes natural lakes or man-made reservoirs.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Lake
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Landlocked Salmon[end_header][start_subHeader]Landlocked salmon includes kokanee and landlocked Chinook salmon.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Landlocked Salmon
rows.Tags: Fin Fish - General

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Limit[end_header][start_subHeader]Refers to daily bag limit and possession limit per person, or boat limit authorized in Sections 27.60(c) and 195, Title 14, CCR.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Limit
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Non-Buoyant Artificial Lure[end_header][start_subHeader]Any artificial lure that sinks in freshwater.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Non-Buoyant Artificial Lure
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Minimum and Maximum Size[end_header][start_subHeader]No fish, mollusks or crustaceans less than the legal minimum size or greater than the maximum legal size (total, fork or alternate) may be possessed, except as otherwise provided. Total length is the longest straight-line measurement from the tip of the head to the end of the longest lobe of the tail. Fork length is the straight-line distance from the tip of the head to the center of the tail fin. Tip of the head shall be the most anterior point on the fish with the mouth closed and the fish lying flat on its side. Alternate length is the straight-line distance from the base of the foremost spine of the first dorsal fin to the end of the longest lobe of the tail. Unless otherwise provided, all fish, mollusks or crustaceans less than the legal minimum size or greater than the maximum legal size must be returned immediately to the water from which they were taken.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Minimum and Maximum Size
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Movement of Live Fish[end_header][start_subHeader]Except as provided in sections 4.00 through 4.30 and 230, live fin fish may not be transported alive from the water where taken.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Movement of Live Fish
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Multiple Hook[end_header][start_subHeader]A hook with two or more points.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Multiple Hook
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Native Reptiles and Amphibians[end_header][start_subHeader]Native reptiles and amphibians are those subspecies, and species, including all color phases, of the classes Reptilia and Amphibia indigenous to California. This definition includes all specimens regardless of their origin even if they were produced in captivity.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Native Reptiles and Amphibians
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Open Season[end_header][start_subHeader]That period of time during which the taking of fish, amphibians, reptiles, mollusks and crustaceans is authorized.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Open Season
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Opening Date and Bag Limit for Boundary Waters[end_header][start_subHeader]Waters, exclusive of their tributaries, on the boundary between areas or districts with different opening dates or limits shall open on the earlier date and have the larger limit unless otherwise specified.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Opening Date and Bag Limit for Boundary Waters
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Sacramento-San Joaquin River Delta[end_header][start_subHeader]The Sacramento-San Joaquin River Delta includes all rivers, sloughs, canals, cuts, forebays, and flooded islands within the area south of Interstate 80 to its junction with Highway 50, and south of Highway 50 via the Pioneer Bridge to its junction with Highway 99, west of Highway 99, north of Interstate 580, 205, and Highway 120, and east of Interstate 680.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Sacramento-San Joaquin River Delta
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Stream (Includes Creeks and Rivers)[end_header][start_subHeader]A stream is a body of water that flows at least periodically or intermittently through a bed or channel having banks and supports fish or other aquatic life. This includes watercourses having a surface or subsurface flow that supports or has supported riparian vegetation.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Stream (Includes Creeks and Rivers)
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Salmon[end_header]
rows.Title: Salmon
rows.Tags: Fin Fish - General

rows.Verbatim: Salmon includes Chinook, coho, pink, chum, and sockeye salmon.
rows.Title: Salmon
rows.Tags: Fin Fish - General

rows.Verbatim: Any person in possession of a recreationally taken salmon with a missing adipose fin (the small, fleshy fin on the back of the fish between the back fin and tail) shall immediately relinquish the head of the salmon, upon request by an authorized agent or employee of the department, to facilitate the recovery of any coded-wire tag. The head may be removed by the fish owner or, if removed by the official department representative, the head shall be removed in a manner to minimize loss of salmon flesh and the salmon shall immediately be returned to the fish owner.
rows.Title: Salmon
rows.Tags: Fin Fish - General

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements.[end_header]
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: Purpose. These regulations are designed to improve recreational fishing effort and catch information in some or all areas where the fisheries operate. Many of these species are of high commercial value, and therefore, additional enforcement mechanisms are needed to improve compliance with existing bag limits and other regulations, and to reduce the potential for poaching.
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: Report card requirements apply to any person fishing for or taking the following species regardless of whether a sport fishing license is required:
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: Salmon, in the anadromous waters of the Klamath, Trinity, and Smith river basins. Anadromous waters are defined in Section 1.04 of these regulations.
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: Steelhead trout.
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: Steelhead trout.
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: White sturgeon.
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: Red abalone.
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: California spiny lobster.
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: General Report Card Requirements.
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: Any person fishing for or taking any of the species identified in this Section shall have in his immediate possession a valid non-transferable report card issued by the department for the particular species. See special exemption regarding possession of report cards for lobster divers in Section 29.91 of these regulations.
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: All entries made on any report card or tag shall be legible and in indelible ink.
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: A report card holder fishing with a one, two, or ten-day sport fishing license, may replace the expired fishing license without purchasing a new report card so long as the report card is still valid.
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: Report cards are not transferable and shall not be transferred to another person. No person shall possess any report card other than his own.
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: A person may only obtain one abalone report card and one sturgeon report card per report card period.
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: Any report card holder who fills in all available lines on his steelhead, salmon or lobster report card shall return or report the card to the department pursuant to subsection 1.74(e) prior to purchasing a second card.
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim:
Data recording and tagging procedures vary between report cards and species. See specific regulations in sections:
5.80 (Inland white sturgeon), 5.87 (North Coast salmon), 5.88 (Steelhead), 27.90 (Ocean white sturgeon),29.16 (Abalone), and 29.91 (Spiny lobster) that apply in addition to the regulations of this Section.
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: Report Card Return and Reporting Requirements
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: Report card holders shall return or report their salmon, steelhead, sturgeon, or abalone report cards to the department pursuant to subsection 1.74(e) by January 31 of the following year.
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: Any report card holder who fails to return or report their salmon, steelhead, sturgeon, or abalone report card to the department by the deadline may be restricted from obtaining the same card in a subsequent license year or may be subject to an additional fee for the issuance of the same card in a subsequent license year.
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: Report card holders shall return or report their lobster report cards pursuant to subsection 1.74(e) by April 30 following the close of the lobster season for which the card was issued.
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: Any report card holder who fails to return or report their lobster report card by April 30 following the close of the lobster season specified on the card shall be subject to a nonrefundable non-return fee specified in Section 701, in addition to the annual report card fee, for the issuance of a lobster report card in the subsequent fishing season.
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: Report Card Return and Reporting Mechanisms:
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: By mail or in person at the address specified on the card. A report card returned by mail shall be postmarked by the date applicable to that card as specified in subsection 1.74(d)(1) or 1.74(d)(2), 5.80(g), or 27.90(g).
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: Online through the department's license sales service website by the date applicable to that card as specified in subsection 1.74(d)(1) or 1.74(d)(2), 5.80(g), or 27.90(g). Report card holders reporting online will be provided a confirmation number upon successful submission. The report card holder must record the provided confirmation number in the space provided on the report card and retain the report card for 90 days after the reporting deadline. Report cards submitted online must be surrendered to the department upon demand.
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: If a report card is submitted by mail and not received by the department, it is considered not returned unless the report card holder reports their report card as lost pursuant to subsection 1.74(f).
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: Lost report cards.
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: Lobster, salmon, sturgeon, and steelhead. Notwithstanding subsection 1.74(c)(5), any report card holder who loses their report card during the report card period for which it is valid may purchase an additional report card by submitting payment to an authorized license agent or department license sales office. Catch information from the lost report card shall not be transferred to the new card. Information from lost lobster, salmon, sturgeon and steelhead report cards shall be reported as specified in subsection 1.74(f)(3).
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: Abalone and sturgeon. Notwithstanding subsection 1.74(c)(5), any report card holder who loses their report card during the period for which it is valid may purchase a replacement report card.
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: The Department may issue a replacement report card for abalone and sturgeon upon completion of the following:
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: Submitting an affidavit to any department license sales office containing all the information specified in subsection 1.74(f)(3)(B); and
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: Submitting payment of the report card fee and the non-refundable replacement-processing fee specified in Section 701.
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: Department staff shall enter the harvest information from the affidavit to the replacement report card.
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: Based on the information provided on the affidavit, department staff shall remove tags reported as used and issue only the number of tags that were reported as unused on the lost original report card.
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: Report card holders shall verify that the harvest information has been accurately transferred from the affidavit to his or her replacement report card.
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: The replacement report card shall be reported pursuant to the requirement for the original report card as specified in subsection 1.74(d). NOTE: the original report card should not be reported.

rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: Reporting requirements. Except for lost abalone and sturgeon report cards for which a replacement card was purchased, all lost report cards shall be reported by the harvest report submission deadline date applicable to that card as specified in subsection 1.74(d)(1) or 1.74(d)(2), 5.80(g), or 27.90(g) by one of the following methods:
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: Online through the department's license sales service website; or
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: Submitting an affidavit, signed under penalty of perjury, to a department license sales office containing the following information:
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: The report card holder's full name, GOID#, and a statement confirming that the originally issued report card is lost and cannot be recovered.
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: A statement containing the report card holder's best recollection of the prior catch records that were entered on the report card that was lost.
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: A statement describing the factual circumstances surrounding the loss of the report card.
rows.Title: Sport Fishing Report Card Requirements
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Salmon Spawning Areas[end_header][start_subHeader]No salmon may be taken or possessed on any salmon spawning area when it is closed to salmon fishing.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Salmon Spawning Areas
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Spearfishing[end_header][start_subHeader]The taking of fish by spear or hand by persons who are in the water and may be using underwater goggles, face plates, breathing tubes, SCUBA or other artificial underwater breathing device.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Spearfishing
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Sunfish[end_header][start_subHeader]Includes bluegill, green sunfish, redear sunfish, pumpkinseed, warmouth, and Sacramento perch.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Sunfish
rows.Tags: Fin Fish - General

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Take[end_header][start_subHeader]Hunt, pursue, catch, capture or kill fish, amphibians, reptiles, mollusks, crustaceans or invertebrates or attempting to do so.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Take
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Titles and Section Numbers[end_header][start_subHeader]All titles and headings used in these regulations are a part thereof. All section numbers cited refer to these regulations unless otherwise specified.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Titles and Section Numbers
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Trout[end_header][start_subHeader]Trout includes all trouts, chars, steelhead, and grayling.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Trout
rows.Tags: Fin Fish - General

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Waste of Fish[end_header][start_subHeader]It is unlawful to cause or permit any deterioration or waste of any fish taken in the waters of this state.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Waste of Fish
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Weight[end_header][start_subHeader]Any object directly or indirectly attached to a fishing line with the purpose of casting or sinking a lure or bait.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Weight
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Fishing Methods: General[end_header]
rows.Title: Fishing Methods - General
rows.Tags: Fin Fish - General

rows.Verbatim: Except as otherwise authorized, all fish may be taken only by angling with one closely attended rod and line or one hand line with not more than three hooks nor more than three artificial lures (each lure may have three hooks attached) attached thereto. Anglers in possession of a valid two-rod stamp and anglers under 16 years of age may use up to two rods in inland waters which regulations provide for the taking of fish by angling, except those waters in which only artificial lures or barbless hooks may be used. See Trout, Salmon and Special Regulations for exceptions.
rows.Title: Fishing Methods - General
rows.Tags: Fin Fish – Gear Restrictions

rows.Verbatim: Snagging is prohibited. Snagging is defined as impaling or attempting to impale a fish in any part of its body other than inside the mouth by use of a hook, hooks, gaff, or other mechanical implement. This definition does not include activities otherwise authorized under these regulations for the lawful use of a gaff, bow and arrow, or spear.
rows.Title: Fishing Methods - General
rows.Tags: Fin Fish – Gear Restrictions

rows.Verbatim: It is unlawful to kill, or retain in possession any fish which has not voluntarily taken the bait or artificial lure inside its mouth. Any fish not taken pursuant to these regulations, shall be released immediately back into the water.
rows.Title: Fishing Methods - General
rows.Tags: Fin Fish – Gear Restrictions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Leader Length Restriction[end_header][start_subHeader]It shall be unlawful to use any configuration of fishing tackle in anadromous waters unless the distance between the terminal hook or terminal lure and any weight attached to the line or leader, whether fixed or sliding, is less than six feet. For purposes of this section, “weight” includes any product used to submerge the line or leader, including non-buoyant artificial flies or artificial lures, but does not include integrated or sinking fly fishing lines, lead core lines used while trolling from a boat, dropper weights used while trolling from a boat, or clipped weights used with downrigger systems.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Leader Length Restriction
rows.Tags: Fin Fish – Gear Restrictions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Use of Gaffs[end_header][start_subHeader]No person shall possess or use a gaff in inland waters, except that a gaff three feet or less in length may be used to land legal-sized fish only by anglers fishing from a boat in the Sacramento River main stem below Deschutes Road Bridge.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Use of Gaffs
rows.Tags: Fin Fish – Gear Restrictions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Special Fishing Methods and Bag Limits--Barrett and Upper Otay Lakes, San Diego County[end_header][start_subHeader]The following fishing methods restrictions and bag limits apply to Barrett Lake and Upper Otay Lake:[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Special Fishing Methods and Bag Limits--Barrett and Upper Otay Lakes, San Diego County
rows.Tags: Fin Fish – Gear Restrictions

rows.Verbatim: Only artificial lures with barbless hooks may be used.
rows.Title: Special Fishing Methods and Bag Limits--Barrett and Upper Otay Lakes, San Diego County
rows.Tags: Fin Fish – Gear Restrictions

rows.Verbatim: The bag limit for all species is zero.
rows.Title: Special Fishing Methods and Bag Limits--Barrett and Upper Otay Lakes, San Diego County
rows.Tags: Fin Fish - Minimum Size Limits, Bag and Possession Limits, and Seasons

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Possession of Illegal Gear[end_header][start_subHeader]Except as otherwise provided, no person shall use or possess, except in his or her home, any landing gear, any nets, except standard landing-type dip nets not exceeding 36 inches in diameter across the net opening and 60 inches in net length/depth, excluding handle, gaffs or spears within 100 yards of any canal, river, stream, lake or reservoir. Non-electronic underwater viewing devices may not be used for taking fish except under the provisions of Section 2.30.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Possession of Illegal Gear
rows.Tags: Fin Fish – Gear Restrictions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Hook And Weight Restrictions.[end_header]

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Bait Fish Capture Methods.[end_header]
rows.Title: Bait Fish Capture Methods
rows.Tags: Fin Fish - General

rows.Verbatim: Approved bait fish may be taken only by hand, with a dip net not exceeding 36 inches in greatest dimension, excluding handle, or with traps not over three feet in greatest dimension. Such bait fish may not be purchased, bartered, sold, transferred or traded; or transported alive from the location where taken. Any other species taken shall be returned to the water immediately. Traps need not be closely attended. Dip net use: A dip net must be hand held, and the motion of a dip net shall be caused only by the physical effort of the operator. A dip net may not be moved through the water by any mechanical force or motorized device.
rows.Title: Bait Fish Capture Methods
rows.Tags: Fin Fish - General

rows.Verbatim: Within the area bounded by Highway 111 on the north and east and Highway 86 on the west and south, approved bait fish may be taken only with dip nets with diagonal mesh size one inch and greater, or by traps in water greater than four feet in depth. Traps may not exceed three feet in greatest dimension. Approved bait fish may not be taken by hand within this area.
rows.Title: Bait Fish Capture Methods
rows.Tags: Fin Fish - General

The angler shall notify the department that he/she has taken and possesses a northern pike by calling the department's CalTip telephone number (1-888-DFG-CALTIP) as soon as possible, but not more than 24 hours after taking the northern pike. rows.Title: Trout

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Hoopa And Yurok Indian Salmon Possession Limit[end_header][start_subHeader]It is unlawful for any person to possess more than one daily bag or possession limit of fish except as follows: Eligible Hoopa Valley and Yurok Reservation Indians, as defined in Chapter 1, Part 250, Title 25, CFR--Indian Fishing, Hoopa Valley Reservation and Yurok Reservation-Department of the Interior; may possess more than two salmon outside boundaries of the Hoopa Valley Reservation, provided:[end_subHeader]

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]North Coast Salmon Report Card Requirement.[end_header]
rows.Title: North Coast Salmon Report Card Requirement
rows.Tags: Other

rows.Verbatim: Report Card Required in Waters of the Klamath-Trinity River System and the Smith River. All anglers must have a North Coast Salmon Report Card in their possession while fishing for or taking salmon in waters of the Klamath-Trinity River System and the Smith River, and must complete and return the card pursuant to regulations in this Section and in Section 1.74.
rows.Title: North Coast Salmon Report Card Requirement
rows.Tags: Other

rows.Verbatim: Prior to beginning fishing activity, the cardholder shall record the month, day, and fishing location on the first available line on the report card.
rows.Title: North Coast Salmon Report Card Requirement
rows.Tags: Other

rows.Verbatim: For the Klamath-Trinity River System: Whenever the cardholder lands (either retains or releases) a Chinook Salmon, the angler shall immediately record whether the fish was an adult or a jack, and whether the fish has an adipose fin present. Whenever the cardholder releases a Coho Salmon, the angler shall immediately record whether the maxillary is present or absent.
rows.Title: North Coast Salmon Report Card Requirement
rows.Tags: Other

rows.Verbatim: For the Smith River: Whenever the cardholder lands (either retains or releases) a Chinook salmon, the angler shall immediately record whether the fish was an adult or a jack, and whether the fish has an adipose fin or left ventral fin present.
rows.Title: North Coast Salmon Report Card Requirement
rows.Tags: Other

rows.Verbatim: Whenever the cardholder moves to another fishing location, the angler shall record the month, day, and location on the next line on the report card.
rows.Title: North Coast Salmon Report Card Requirement
rows.Tags: Other

rows.Verbatim: In the Klamath-Trinity River System and Smith River, a jack Chinook salmon is defined as any Chinook salmon that is less than 22 inches total length.
rows.Title: North Coast Salmon Report Card Requirement
rows.Tags: Other

rows.Verbatim: In the event an angler fills in all lines and returns a North Coast Salmon Report Card, an additional card may be purchased. See Section 1.74.
rows.Title: North Coast Salmon Report Card Requirement
rows.Tags: Other

rows.Verbatim: The annual fee for the North Coast Salmon Report Card is specified in Section 701(b).
rows.Title: North Coast Salmon Report Card Requirement
rows.Tags: Other

rows.Verbatim: Steelhead Fishing Report and Restoration Card Required. All anglers must have a Steelhead Fishing Report and Restoration Card in their possession while fishing for or taking steelhead in anadromous waters, as defined in Section 1.04. Anglers must complete and return the card pursuant to regulations in this Section and in Section 1.74. For purposes of these regulations, a steelhead trout is defined as any rainbow trout greater than 16 inches in length found in anadromous waters.

rows.Tags: Fin Fish - General

rows.Verbatim: Prior to beginning fishing activity, the cardholder must record the month, day, and location code on the first available line on the report card.

rows.Verbatim: When a hatchery steelhead is retained, the cardholder must immediately mark the appropriate field.

rows.Verbatim: When the cardholder moves to another location code, or finishes fishing for the day, the angler must immediately record on the card the number of wild and hatchery steelhead that were released from that location.

rows.Verbatim: In the event an angler fills in all lines and returns a Steelhead Fishing Report and Restoration Card, an additional card must be purchased to continue to fish for steelhead. See Section 1.74.
rows.Title: Steelhead Report And Restoration Card Requirements For Inland Waters
rows.Tags: Fin Fish - General

rows.Verbatim: The annual fee for the Steelhead Fishing Report and Restoration Card is specified in Section 7380 of the Fish and Game Code.
rows.Title: Steelhead Report And Restoration Card Requirements For Inland Waters

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Southern District Definition[end_header][start_subHeader]The Sierra District consists of all of Modoc, Lassen, Shasta, Sierra, Plumas, Alpine, Inyo and Mono counties; Tulare County east of the west boundaries of Sequoia National Forest and Sequoia National Park; Fresno County east of the west boundaries of Sierra and Sequoia National Forests (excluding Pine Flat Lake); Madera County east of the west boundary of Sierra National Forest; Mariposa, Tuolumne, Calaveras, Amador, El Dorado, Placer and Nevada counties east of Highway 49 (excluding Don Pedro, McClure and New Melones lakes); the portion of Siskiyou County southeast of a line drawn between Mt. Eddy and the Black Butte summit railroad crossing of Interstate 5 and east of Interstate 5 between the railroad crossing and Weed and east of Highway 97 between Weed and the Oregon border; and Tehama County excluding Black Butte Lake. Those waters excluded above are part of the Valley District (see Section 6.36).[end_subHeader]

rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Sierra District Definition[end_header][start_subHeader]The Sierra District consists of all of Modoc, Lassen, Shasta, Sierra, Plumas, Alpine, Inyo and Mono counties; Tulare County east of the west boundaries of Sequoia National Forest and Sequoia National Park; Fresno County east of the west boundaries of Sierra and Sequoia National Forests (excluding Pine Flat Lake); Madera County east of the west boundary of Sierra National Forest; Mariposa, Tuolumne, Calaveras, Amador, El Dorado, Placer and Nevada counties east of Highway 49 (excluding Don Pedro, McClure and New Melones lakes); the portion of Siskiyou County southeast of a line drawn between Mt. Eddy and the Black Butte summit railroad crossing of Interstate 5 and east of Interstate 5 between the railroad crossing and Weed and east of Highway 97 between Weed and the Oregon border; and Tehama County excluding Black Butte Lake. Those waters excluded above are part of the Valley District (see Section 6.36).[end_subHeader]

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Valley District Definition[end_header][start_subHeader]The Valley District consists of all of Butte, Colusa, Glenn, Kern, Kings, Merced, Sacramento, San Joaquin, Solano, Stanislaus, Sutter, Yolo and Yuba counties; Tulare County west of the west boundaries of Sequoia National Forest and Sequoia National Park; Fresno County west of the west boundaries of Sierra and Sequoia National Forests (including all of Pine Flat Lake); Madera County west of the west boundary of the Sierra National Forest; Amador, Calaveras, El Dorado, Mariposa, Nevada, Placer and Tuolomne counties west of Highway 49 (including all of Don Pedro, McClure and New Melones lakes); that portion of Alameda County which is both east of Interstate 680 and north of Interstate 580; and all of Contra Costa County east of Interstate 680 and that portion of Contra Costa County which is both north of Highway 4 and east of Interstate 80; and all of Black Butte Lake.[end_subHeader]

rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]Colorado River District Definition[end_header][start_subHeader]The Colorado River District consists of Imperial County and those portions of Riverside and San Bernardino counties lying south and east of the following line: Starting at the intersection of Highway 86 with the north boundary of Imperial County; north along Highway 86 to its intersection with Interstate 10; east along Interstate 10 to its intersection with Cottonwood Springs Road; north along Cottonwood Springs Road and the Mecca Dale Road to Amboy; east along old Highway 66 to its intersection with Interstate 40; east along Interstate 40 to its intersection with Highway 95; and north along Highway 95 to the California-Nevada boundary. All of the Coachella Canal and Lake Cahuilla are included in this District.[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: Colorado River District Definition
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: [start_header]District General Regulations[end_header][start_subHeader]Unless otherwise provided, waters shown as open to hatchery trout and hatchery steelhead fishing in subsections (a)  through (g) below, are open to fishing for other species. Gear restrictions listed in this section apply to the take of all  species of fish unless otherwise noted. Every body of water listed in subsections (a) through (g) of Section 7.00 (below)  is closed to all fishing, except during the open season as shown.  Unless otherwise provided, waters closed to hatchery trout and hatchery steelhead fishing are closed to fishing for all  other species, except that these closures do not apply to fishing for amphibians (see Section 5.05), freshwater clams  (see Section 5.20), crayfish (see Section 5.35), and lamprey (see Section 5.40), using legal fishing methods other than  hook-and-line fishing, and saltwater clams, crabs, ghost shrimp, and blue mud shrimp (see Ocean Regulations Booklet  sections 29.20 to 29.87). Crabs may only be taken using hoop nets or by hand, and Dungeness crab may only be taken  withinthe North Coast District and Sonoma and Mendocino counties.  Daily bag and possession limits, unless otherwise provided, mean the total number of hatchery trout and hatchery  steelhead. Unless otherwise provided, no more than one daily bag limit may be possessed. Coho (silver) salmon may  not be taken in any of the waters of the State. Incidentally hooked Coho (silver) salmon must be immediately released  unharmed to the waters where they are hooked. In waters where the bag limit for hatchery trout and hatchery steelhead is zero, fish for which the bag limit is zero must be released unharmed, and should not be removed from the  water. These waters may also be subject to restrictions on fishing methods and gear (sections 2.00 through 2.45), fishing  hours (Section 3.00), and the use of bait (sections 4.00 through 4.30). *Hatchery trout or steelhead have a healed adipose fin clip (adipose fin is absent). Unless otherwise provided, all other  trout and steelhead must be immediately released. Wild trout or steelhead are those not showing a healed adipose  fin clip (adipose fin present).[end_subHeader]
rows.Title: District General Regulations
rows.Tags: Fin Fish - General

rows.Verbatim: General Provisions:
rows.Title: Alphabetical List of Hatchery Trout, Hatchery Steelhead, and Salmon Waters with Special Fishing Regulations
rows.Tags: Fin Fish - General

rows.Verbatim: Every body of water listed in subsection (b) is closed to the take of hatchery trout, hatchery steelhead, and salmon and to fishing for these species, unless otherwise noted.
rows.Title: Alphabetical List of Hatchery Trout, Hatchery Steelhead, and Salmon Waters with Special Fishing Regulations
rows.Tags: Fin Fish - General

rows.Verbatim: Every body of water listed in subsection (b) is closed to all fishing except during the open season as shown. Unless otherwise provided, waters shown as open to hatchery trout, hatchery steelhead, and salmon fishing in subsection (b) are open to fishing for other species. Gear restrictions listed in this section apply to the take of all species of fish unless otherwise noted.
rows.Title: Alphabetical List of Hatchery Trout, Hatchery Steelhead, and Salmon Waters with Special Fishing Regulations
rows.Tags: Fin Fish - General

rows.Verbatim: Unless otherwise provided, waters closed to hatchery trout, hatchery steelhead, or salmon fishing are closed to fishing for all other species, except that these closures do not apply to fishing for amphibians (see Section 5.05), freshwater clams (see Section 5.20), crayfish (see Section 5.35), and lamprey (see Section 5.40), using legal fishing methods other than hook-and-line fishing, and saltwater clams, crabs, ghost shrimp, and blue mud shrimp (see Ocean Regulations Booklet sections 29.20 to 29.87). Crabs may only be taken using hoop nets or by hand, and Dungeness crab may not be taken within the North Coast District and Sonoma and Mendocino counties.
rows.Title: Alphabetical List of Hatchery Trout, Hatchery Steelhead, and Salmon Waters with Special Fishing Regulations
rows.Tags: Fin Fish - General

rows.Verbatim: Unless otherwise provided, it is unlawful to possess more than one daily bag limit.
rows.Title: Alphabetical List of Hatchery Trout, Hatchery Steelhead, and Salmon Waters with Special Fishing Regulations
rows.Tags: Fin Fish - General

rows.Verbatim: The waters in subsection (b) may also be subject to restrictions on fishing methods and gear (Sections 2.00 through 2.45), fishing hours (Section 3.00), and the use of bait (Sections 4.00 through 4.30).

rows.Verbatim: General Provisions:

rows.Verbatim: Every body of water listed in subsection (b) is closed to all fishing except during the open season as shown. Unless otherwise provided, waters shown as open to trout fishing in subsection (b), are open to fishing for other species. Gear restrictions listed in this section apply to the take of all species of fish unless otherwise noted.
rows.Title: Alphabetical List of Trout Waters with Special Fishing Regulations
rows.Tags: Fin Fish - General

rows.Verbatim: Daily bag and possession limits, unless otherwise noted, mean the total number of trout.
rows.Title: Alphabetical List of Trout Waters with Special Fishing Regulations
rows.Tags: Fin Fish - General

rows.Verbatim: Unless otherwise provided, it is unlawful to possess more than one daily bag limit.
rows.Title: Alphabetical List of Trout Waters with Special Fishing Regulations
rows.Tags: Fin Fish - General

rows.Verbatim: Eel River, Mad River, Mattole River, Redwood Creek, Smith River and Van Duzen River. Stream closures: Special Low Flow Conditions.
rows.Title: Low-Flow Restrictions
rows.Tags: Other

rows.Verbatim: September 1 through April 30:
rows.Title: Low-Flow Restrictions
rows.Tags: Other

rows.Verbatim: Any of the stream reaches listed in subsections (a)(2) through (8) below shall be closed to all angling on Tuesday and Wednesday when the department determines that the flow on the previous Monday at any of the designated gauging stations is less than the minimum flows set forth in subsections (a)(2) through (8).
rows.Title: Low-Flow Restrictions
rows.Tags: Other

rows.Verbatim: Any of the stream reaches listed in subsections (a)(2) through (8) below shall be closed to all angling on Thursday and Friday when the department determines that the flow on the previous Wednesday at any of the designated gauging stations is less than the minimum flows set forth in subsections (a)(2) through (8).
rows.Title: Low-Flow Restrictions
rows.Tags: Other

rows.Verbatim: Any of the stream reaches listed in subsections (a)(2) through (8) below shall be closed to all angling from Saturday through Monday when the department determines that the flow on the previous Friday at any of the designated gauging stations is less than the minimum flows set forth in subsections (a)(2) through (8).
rows.Title: Low-Flow Restrictions
rows.Tags: Other

rows.Verbatim: Notwithstanding subsections (a)(1)(A) through (C), the department may close or keep a stream reach closed to fishing when the minimum flow is exceeded on the scheduled flow determination day if the department is reasonably assured that the stream flow is likely to decrease below the minimum flow as specified in subsections (a)(2) through (8) before or on the next flow-determination date.
rows.Title: Low-Flow Restrictions
rows.Tags: Other

rows.Verbatim: The department may reopen a stream at any time during a closed period if the minimum flow as specified in subsections (a)(2) through (8) is exceeded and the department is reasonably assured that it will remain above the minimum flow until the next scheduled Monday, Wednesday, or Friday flow determination. The department shall make information available to the public by a webpage updated, as necessary, no later than 1:00 p.m. each Monday, Wednesday, and Friday as to whether any stream will be open or closed to fishing. It shall be the responsibility of the angler to use the webpage designated in the sport fishing regulations booklet to obtain information on the status of any stream.  Check the Department's regulations page at www.wildlife.ca.gov/regulations for Low-Flow Restrictions and Information. Or at wildlife.ca.gov/Fishing/Inland/Low-Flow.
rows.Title: Low-Flow Restrictions
rows.Tags: Other

rows.Verbatim: Transgenic.
rows.Title: Transgenic.
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: An animal whose genome has been deliberately altered, modified, or engineered, through means not possible under natural conditions, by insertion of a foreign gene or genes using genetic engineering methods.
rows.Title: Transgenic.
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: An animal is transgenic if its chromosomes contain artificially transferred genetic material from any other organism or a laboratory construct, regardless of whether the original source's genetic material was altered, modified or engineered prior to insertion, or whether the originally transferred genetic material was inherited through normal reproduction.
rows.Title: Transgenic.
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: Methods of producing transgenic animals may include, but are not limited to, recombinant DNA and RNA techniques, cell fusion, micro- and macro-encapsulation, introduction of a foreign gene, or gene knock-in.
rows.Title: Transgenic.
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: Any progeny of a transgenic animal is transgenic within the meaning of this section.
rows.Title: Transgenic.
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: Notwithstanding subsection (a) above, an animal is not transgenic within the meaning of this section if:
rows.Title: Transgenic.
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: It is an aquatic animal species produced through breeding, conjugation, fermentation, hybridization, in vitro fertilization, or tissue culture and no transgenic organisms are involved;
rows.Title: Transgenic.
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: It is an aquatic animal species produced through whole genome ploidy manipulation; or
rows.Title: Transgenic.
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: The foreign gene or genes in the animal is the result of therapeutic treatment with a DNA vaccine.
rows.Title: Transgenic.
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: Notwithstanding subsection 671(c)(11), a transgenic aquatic animal is not detrimental, and therefore not subject to regulation under Section 671 and subsection 671.1(a)(8), if all of the following apply:
rows.Title: Transgenic.
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: It is a live tropical marine or freshwater animal that will not be utilized for research purposes, human consumption, or bait purposes and will be maintained in a closed system and not placed in waters of the state;
rows.Title: Transgenic.
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: The applicant, which may be a person or entity, seeking to import, distribute, possess, and sell the transgenic aquatic animal in California has submitted to the department the application and fee specified in Section 703.
rows.Title: Transgenic.
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

rows.Verbatim: The department has determined in writing, based on the information provided pursuant to subsection (b)(2), and any other relevant credible scientific information in the possession of the department or submitted to the department, that the presence of the transgenic aquatic animal within California poses no reasonably foreseeable risk to native fish, wildlife, or plants.
rows.Title: Transgenic.
rows.Tags: General Provisions and Definitions

Methods of take: Only one single point, single shank, barbless hook shall be used on a line when taking sturgeon. The sturgeon must voluntarily take the bait or lure inside its mouth. No sturgeon may 
be taken by trolling, snagging or by the use of firearms. Sturgeon may not be gaffed, nor shall any person use any type of firearm or snare to take any sturgeon.  For the purposes of this section, a snare is a flexible loop made from any material that can be tightened like a noose around any part of the fish.
rows.Title: Inland White Sturgeon
rows.Tags: Fin Fish – Gear Restrictions

rows.Verbatim: Handling and removal from water. Any sturgeon greater than 60 inches fork length may not be removed from the water and shall be released immediately. Sturgeon of any size shall not be held out of water suspended by the gills, gill plates, mouth, or solely by the tail, and shall not be dragged across the ground, boat decks, or piers. Lip gripper devices shall not be used on sturgeon.
rows.Title: Inland White Sturgeon
rows.Tags: Fin Fish - Minimum Size Limits, Bag and Possession Limits, and Seasons
